title: Whale-Proof Alert Network for Longline Boats
one_liner: A reciprocal, location-fuzzed alert network that lets sablefish and halibut longliners warn each other about orcas and sperm whales without giving up their fishing spots.
customer: Owner-operators of IFQ longline vessels in the Gulf of Alaska, Southeast and Bering Sea (roughly several hundred boats), sold through fishermen's associations, at $600-1,500 per vessel per season. Expansion buyers are pelagic longline fleets worldwide (tuna, toothfish) that also lose fish to whales.
problem: Whales strip the gear as it comes up, and bad sets lose a double-digit percentage of the catch. The whales learn the sound of your hauler and follow the boat, and sometimes the fleet. Every skipper knows it, but sightings travel only on private VHF codes and phone calls. Reporting a whale reveals where you are fishing. The boat that 'brings the whales' gets blamed. So the fleet's best early-warning data is never pooled.
solution: An app and text-message bot that runs over Garmin inReach, Iridium or Starlink. A skipper sends a one-line report ('killer whales, 8 mi of hall X'). The system publishes only a fuzzed geohash after a delay and strips vessel identity. You can see alerts only if you report (reciprocity credits). A model adds depredation-risk scores by area, soak time, season and haul timing. A playbook covers acoustic hygiene: hauler noise, set and haul timing, gear moves. An optional hydrophone kit comes later. Anonymized data goes to researchers, associations and insurers.
why_now: Quotas are tight and sablefish and halibut prices are well below their highs, so every whale-eaten pound matters more. Satellite texting from the wheelhouse is now cheap and near-universal (Starlink, inReach). Researchers have shown that whales learn from boat acoustics, which gives the fleet a reason to trust a shared system. Fishermen have also been moving toward pots to cope with whales, which shows they will pay for anything that works.
revenue_model: Per-vessel seasonal subscription ($600-1,500), association-level enterprise licenses, and anonymized depredation data sold to research programs, regulators and insurers. Upside is global pelagic longline fleets that all have the same depredation problem.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not detection technology, it is mechanism design. Skippers guard spots and fear blame, so they share whale sightings only in private. A network that gives value only to reporters, blurs location and time, and hides identity solves that. It is a game-theory product disguised as a whale app. Whale behavior is also fleet-learned, so tracking anonymized boat signatures over time is a data asset nobody else has.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 skippers in Sitka, Kodiak and Homer through the longline associations. The sablefish season closes mid-November, so use the winter to run it as a manual pilot: a group text plus a spreadsheet plus a simple map, paying $100 for reports. Interview skippers about how they signal each other today. Draft the fuzzing rules with them. Sell pre-season subscriptions in Feb-Mar and go live for the March opening.

title: Substitute-Plan Binders for Retiring Business Owners
one_liner: Retired teachers interview 60+ owner-operators and write a 'sub plan' any stranger could use to run the shop for a week, sold through business brokers.
customer: Owner-operators aged 60+ of $300k-$3M revenue businesses that depend on the owner's head (HVAC and plumbing, vet and dental practices, hardware stores, salons, daycares, landscaping). The channel and co-payer is the business broker, plus SBA lenders, CPAs and estate attorneys. Acquirers such as search-fund and ETA buyers pay later for a 'day-one' version.
problem: About 40% of small business owners are boomers, and roughly 6 million businesses will change hands by 2035. Around 70% of listed small businesses never sell, and about half of owners have no succession plan. Buyers and lenders can't underwrite what lives only in the owner's memory. Owners refuse to write SOPs, but they will talk for hours. Brokers watch listings die at the diligence stage because 'the business is the owner.'
solution: Two half-day interview sessions plus a video walk-through of the shop. Teachers are trained to draw knowledge out of people with questions. The output is a 20-40 page Sub Plan written in the classroom genre. It covers the daily schedule and routines, where the keys and passwords are, the 'kids to watch' (the difficult customer, the vendor who needs a call before noon, the employee who needs praise), emergency procedures, a first-hour and first-week script, and 'what NOT to do.' The org chart is drawn as a seating chart showing who actually influences whom. Then comes the sub test. A stranger runs a 4-hour shift from the binder, and every gap they hit gets fixed. The result becomes a diligence exhibit in the sale memorandum. AI transcription and structuring keep labor cost low, and the human elicitation stays the scarce part.
why_now: Coverage of the 'Great Ownership Transfer' peaked in 2026 (McKinsey, Forbes and others). First-time buyers via SBA 7(a) loans and search funds are flooding the market and underwriting transferability. AI transcription and structuring dropped the cost of capturing tacit knowledge by roughly 10x in the last two years. The oldest boomers turn 80 this year, and estate attorneys are seeing more 'owner died, business worthless in 90 days' cases.
revenue_model: $2,400 flat per binder, usually rolled into the broker's listing package. Brokers get a referral credit of about $300. There is a $49/month 'living binder' update plan. Buyers can pay $1,500 for a post-close rewrite. There is a $600 add-on for estate attorneys covering an 'if I'm hit by a bus' version.
non_obvious_insight: The sub plan is the most battle-tested knowledge-transfer document in existence. Every teacher has written hundreds of them for a stranger with 30 unpredictable kids and six hours. No consultant has that reps count. The real asset in a small business is the informal 'kids to watch' list, which never appears in any SOP. Sellers don't fail because they lack documents. They fail because nobody asked the right questions in the right order.
first_30_days: Recruit 4-5 retired teachers who like interviewing. Pick one metro and pitch 20 business brokers with one offer: 'give me your stalest listing, the one that has sat 9+ months, and I'll run a free pilot binder.' Do 3 free pilots in exchange for testimonials and an intro to the broker's next 5 listings. Then charge $2,400. Add SCORE chapters, SBDCs and estate attorneys as second-wave channels.

title: Demumu With a Body: Paid Welfare-Check Responders
one_liner: Parent-paid check-in safety for Chinese-, Indian- and Korean-speaking students and migrants living alone abroad, where a missed check-in triggers a paid local door-knock instead of an email to someone 10,000 km away.
customer: Parents (in China, India, Korea) of students and young professionals living alone abroad, who pay about $6/month plus about $45 per dispatched welfare check. Universities' international offices are a secondary channel.
problem: The viral Chinese app 'Are You Dead?' (renamed Demumu) proves demand for solo-living safety, but its only action is an email alert to two emergency contacts. For migrants those contacts are usually parents or friends in another city or country who cannot physically check. China has more than 125 million one-person households, projected at 200 million by 2030. About two-thirds of solo dwellers are aged 20-59, i.e. young migrants rather than the elderly.
solution: A student-controlled check-in app (student chooses the circle, parents pay). After a missed check-in, the escalation is: push, SMS and call, then roommates and landlord, and finally a vetted local responder who does a door-knock with a photo-verified report and can escalate to the local non-emergency welfare-check line or emergency services. The responders are recruited from the same student and gig pool as China's 'companion economy' providers, in host cities such as Boston, London, Sydney and Toronto.
why_now: Demumu's rebrand and global launch in January 2026 put the format on top of app charts in China and among paid utilities in the West, so users now trust the idea. Anyone can clone the basic check-in app in a weekend, since it reportedly cost about ¥1,500 to build. The defensible layer is physical response, which the viral app doesn't have. A 50 billion yuan ($7.4B) Chinese 'companionship economy' shows that people pay for on-demand human presence.
revenue_model: $6/month parent subscription, plus $45 per dispatch or prepaid packs of two. Later, university international-office licensing and insurer partnerships (travel and student health plans).
non_obvious_insight: The buyer is not the solo-liver. It is the anxious relative paying $30-60k a year in tuition, for whom $6/month is trivial. The viral product's critical gap is what happens after the alert. Evidence: Demumu reportedly cost about ¥1,500 ($210) to build, alerts two emergency contacts by email, most solo dwellers are 20-59, and there are 125 million one-person households (https://theconversation.com/are-you-dead-chinas-viral-app-reveals-a-complex-reality-of-solo-living-and-changing-social-ties-274536). It was the top paid app in China at 8 yuan and hit the top paid utilities in Australia (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/14/chinese-app-are-you-dead-to-change-name-after-surge-in-popularity and https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-01-15/are-you-dead-app-changes-name-demumu/106228484). Companion providers already earn 3,000-5,000 yuan/month and one hiking firm grew from under 10 to 370 workers (https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/hiking-hotpot-lonely-consumers-china-031456787.html), so a responder supply pool exists.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: White-label a check-in flow (Twilio plus a simple app or LINE/WeChat mini-program) and write parent-facing Chinese copy. Recruit and vet 10 responders (graduate students) in 3 cities, with a code of conduct and background check. Days 8-20: Post on Xiaohongshu 'studying abroad' and 'parents of overseas students' and in WeChat parent groups, offering a free first month. Days 21-30: Convert 100 parent subscribers, run at least 3 real dispatches and publish the anonymized outcomes. Test privacy and consent wording with 20 students, because the student must opt in and control the circle. Assumption to test: parents' willingness to pay, and student acceptance.

title: Medicaid Work-Rule Retention for Hospitals and Plans
one_liner: A text-first service that proves work hours and exemptions on behalf of Medicaid members, paid per retained member by the hospitals and health plans that would otherwise lose them.
customer: Safety-net hospitals, FQHC networks and Medicaid managed-care plans in expansion states. They pay roughly $4-12 per retained member per month or a fee per successful report.
problem: Under the 2025 budget law (OBBBA), expansion adults aged 19-64 must document about 80 hours a month of work, school or volunteering, or prove an exemption, with more frequent renewals. Deadlines start no later than January 1, 2027, with limited state extensions. Arkansas in 2018 showed that people mostly lost coverage from reporting failures, not from ineligibility. Members lose coverage over paperwork. Hospitals and plans then lose revenue and absorb uncompensated care.
solution: A retention layer that sits on the member side. It works over SMS and WhatsApp in multiple languages. It connects to the member's payroll, gig-platform earnings, school enrollment or caregiver records to auto-assemble monthly proof. It screens for the many exemptions (medically frail, parents of young children, substance-use treatment, recent release) and generates provider attestation letters from the clinic's own visit. It submits in each state's format, using portal automation and mail-in where needed. It nags before deadlines. A dashboard shows the plan or hospital which members are at risk before the coverage cliff. The same engine later covers SNAP work rules.
why_now: The law was signed in July 2025, and federal guidance and state build-outs are happening now for the 2027 start. Some states, such as Georgia with Pathways, already run work-reporting programs. The large incumbents (state-agency contractors) build for the state side, not for retention on the member side. Hospital CFOs are modeling large expansion-population losses this budget cycle. LLM agents plus computer-use can drive dozens of clunky state portals that never had APIs. Gig and payroll data connections make proof of hours automatic.
revenue_model: Per-member-per-month retention fee, or per-successful-report fee, paid by hospitals, FQHCs and plans. Later, state contracts and a SNAP work-requirement product on the same infrastructure.
non_obvious_insight: The payer is neither the patient nor the state. It is whoever loses revenue when a member drops. The failure is documentation friction, not eligibility. The cheapest evidence source is the member's own gig or payroll account plus the clinic visit itself, which can collect exemption proof for free.
first_30_days: Choose one state with an early or waiver-driven start and a large FQHC association. Meet revenue-cycle and financial-counseling leads at 5 FQHCs and hospitals. Publish a free state-by-state 'Am I exempt? Do my hours count?' checker to generate leads. Run a manual SMS concierge pilot with 200 members using a spreadsheet and volunteers, and measure on-time reporting rate. Convert the best result into a signed letter of intent for a per-retained-member fee.

title: Roof Reserve for the ACV Roof Coverage Gap
one_liner: A monthly plan that pre-funds a fixed-price roof replacement, covering the depreciation gap created when owners move to ACV roof coverage.
customer: Homeowners with roofs over 10-12 years old in hail and wildfire states (CO, TX, CA), sold through independent agents and roofers.
problem: Fannie and Freddie (LL-2026-03, Mar 18 2026) now accept actual-cash-value roof coverage. Carriers can cut premiums by moving old roofs to ACV, but the depreciation gap lands on the owner at claim time, often $20-40K. Nobody sells the gap. Hail drives 26-54% of Colorado premiums, so this happens often.
solution: 'Roof Reserve': a $40-90/month prepaid service plan that locks a fixed-price Class 4 or wildfire-rated roof replacement with a vetted roofer and funds the ACV gap after a covered claim. It is structured as a prepaid home-service contract, not insurance (check state rules). Agents earn commission, and the ACV option becomes easier to sell.
why_now: The GSE rule change came in March 2026, and reinsurance softening lets carriers offer ACV options. Colorado now credits documented mitigation.
revenue_model: Monthly subscription plus float, and a 3-6% referral or pre-sold job margin from roofers.
non_obvious_insight: When a regulator loosens a rule to lower premiums, the risk does not disappear. It moves onto the owner's balance sheet, and roofers value a pre-funded pipeline.
first_30_days: Partner with 2 Colorado agencies and 1 roofer. Sell 30 plans to owners whose 12-plus-year roofs are being moved to ACV at renewal. Get a legal read on service-contract versus insurance classification first.

title: Monetization Compliance-as-Code for Free-to-Play Studios
one_liner: A linter that reads a studio's store and gacha configuration and flags per-country, per-age-band violations, with an auditable rulebook curated by counsel.
customer: Mid-size free-to-play mobile and PC studios and publishers (10-300 staff) selling in the EU, UK, Brazil, Australia and US states.
problem: Rules diverge fast. Brazil's 2025 child-protection law restricts loot boxes for minors (in force in 2026), the EU consumer authorities set 2025 principles on virtual currency pricing, and an EU Digital Fairness Act proposal is expected around late 2026. Roblox age tiers and Discord age checks add age-band segmentation. Studios rely on $400-600 per hour legal memos and hand-checked spreadsheets.
solution: Ingest offer tables, gacha odds, currency bundles and subscription flows from LiveOps exports or APIs. Flag violations per market and age band against a versioned rulebook, produce audit-ready evidence, and gate builds in CI.
why_now: Brazil's restrictions took effect in 2026, the Digital Fairness Act is in the pipeline, and platform age tiers force age-aware storefronts. Enforcement history (Epic's FTC settlements) shows the cost of missing this.
revenue_model: $500-3,000 per month per title, $5-15k onboarding, and a premium tier with counsel-reviewed rule updates.
non_obvious_insight: Games compliance is sold as legal advice, but violations live in JSON: drop tables, prices, labels and flows. That is machine-checkable, law firms sell memos, and nobody ships a linter.
first_30_days: Have a games-regulatory lawyer co-write a 4-market rulebook. Build a linter for one config format (Remote Config plus a gacha CSV). Offer free audits to 10 mobile studios and convert 2 to $1k per month.

title: Camera-to-Courtroom Evidence Provenance for Small Firms
one_liner: A capture app and export service that timestamps and cryptographically signs photos, video, texts and voicemails at collection, packaged with an authentication affidavit for court.
customer: Family-law, employment, landlord-tenant and personal-injury firms with up to 10 attorneys, their clients, legal-aid groups and HR investigators.
problem: Deepfakes make every screenshot and clip attackable. Courts and rule-makers are debating standards for machine-generated and possibly fabricated evidence (background, verify), and opposing counsel increasingly says 'that could be AI'. Honest clients then need a forensic expert at thousands of dollars per item to prove authenticity.
solution: Mobile capture that uses C2PA Content Credentials where phones support them (Pixel 10 added camera-level signing in 2025, background, verify) with a fallback for other devices, an SMS, WhatsApp and iMessage exporter with hash chaining, RFC 3161 trusted timestamps, chain-of-custody logs, and a one-click authentication package with a declaration template and a verifier page for the court. Optional expert-declaration add-on.
why_now: Mainstream phones gained hardware-backed provenance in 2025, judicial scrutiny of AI-generated evidence rose through 2025-26, and timestamping and signing infrastructure is now near-free.
revenue_model: $9-29 per case pack, $99-299/month per firm, and $250-500 per expert add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The generative-AI problem for law is not only fake evidence getting in, but real evidence being dismissed. Provenance at creation is a right-of-reply tool for the party with fewer resources, so the customer is the weaker litigant's lawyer.
first_30_days: Ship the capture app and message exporter, pilot with 15 family-law solos, get a forensic examiner to co-sign the package and stage a mock authentication hearing with a law-school clinic. Charge $99/month afterward.

title: Notary for AI Agents' Authority to Sign
one_liner: A registry of signed, scoped, revocable 'mandates' that let a company's AI agents prove to counterparties what they may commit to, with a legal opinion and an insurer behind each.
customer: SMBs and mid-market firms deploying purchasing, AR/AP, sales-ops and scheduling agents (finance and ops leads), the fintech and AP-automation platforms embedding those agents, and the vendors on the receiving end.
problem: Agents now email vendors, accept quotes, change orders and click 'I agree'. Counterparties cannot tell whether an agent had authority, whose it is, or its spend limit, and companies cannot prove afterward what they authorized. Contract-formation doctrine (electronic-agent provisions, apparent authority) predates this. Payment protocols carry payment mandates, not authority to bind.
solution: Phase one: a legal template and JSON mandate schema (principal, agent identity, scope by category and counterparty, dollar cap, expiry, escalation), signed as verifiable credentials, with a public verify API and a revocation registry, an audit log, and a law-firm opinion letter on enforceability for the first US states. Any counterparty agent can call a check_mandate MCP tool. Phase two: an MGA-backed insurance product for agent commitments up to the mandate cap.
why_now: MCP and agent-payment protocols emerged in 2025 and small-firm agent adoption is visible now (60+ firms on MyCase's connector in one month), yet the contract-authority layer between payments and law has no owner (background, verify).
revenue_model: $50-500/month per business, per-verification fees for high-volume counterparties, an insurance premium share, and $10-25k enterprise opinion-letter packages.
non_obvious_insight: Payment rails answer 'can this agent pay?' while the law asks 'was it authorized to bind?', and that depends on documented delegation, the same problem powers of attorney and corporate resolutions solved for humans. Whoever sets the schema counterparties check becomes the standard.
first_30_days: Draft the mandate schema and template with a partner law firm and publish an open spec. Pilot with five procurement or AP-agent startups, ship the verify API, get three design partners to put an authority header in agent emails, and open talks with two MGAs.

title: Fifteen-Minute Court Reporting for Family Law Hearings
one_liner: Remove the half-day minimum by dispatching remote stenographers into many short hearings per day, so a family-law litigant gets a certified record of a 15-minute hearing for about $100.
customer: California family law and probate attorneys and solo practitioners. Self-represented litigants reached through DV legal aid organizations and family law facilitators. Legal aid groups buying bulk credits. Later, county courts contracting to meet the new duty to provide records to indigent litigants.
problem: California logged roughly 3 million civil, family and probate hearings without a verbatim record between April 2023 and March 2026, about 7 in 10. Without a record, appeals of custody and restraining-order rulings fail, because the appellant cannot show error. Private reporters charge $250-$500+ appearance minimums, since a reporter can wait 2-3 hours for a 12-minute calendar item. Nobody pays that for a routine hearing. In 2026 the California Supreme Court (Family Violence Appellate Project v. Superior Court) held that courts must give indigent litigants an official verbatim record on request, and courts do not have the reporters to comply.
solution: A dispatch platform that reads court calendars, predicts when each matter will be called from historical hearing-type durations per department, and pages a remote reporter into the court's Zoom or Teams feed only for the minutes needed. One reporter covers 8-12 short hearings a day across departments. Deliver a certified transcript in 24-72 hours, with an AI first draft for the reporter to scope. Price is a flat $95 for hearings up to 15 minutes and about $8 per page beyond that. Start where remote appearance and remote reporting are allowed (California's AB 3013 authorizes remote reporting, and each court's procedures need checking). Pitch courts on per-department-day capacity at a discount to staffing a full-time reporter.
why_now: The 2026 California Supreme Court ruling creates a legal duty courts cannot currently meet. AB 3013 (2024) opened remote reporting. The workforce is projected to be about 5,500 reporters short by 2030. Family courts are widely on video. Reporter dead time is a scheduling problem that software can solve.
revenue_model: Per-hearing fees paid by attorneys and litigants. Bulk credits funded by legal aid and foundation grants. Later B2G contracts priced per courtroom-day. The reporter keeps about 55-60% of each hearing fee, which beats their typical hourly yield because dead time is eliminated.
non_obvious_insight: The reporter shortage is partly a utilization problem. In a busy family calendar department, a reporter may write 2-3 hours of a 7-hour day and wait the rest. Remote hopping sells that dead time to several litigants at once, so the price can fall 70% while the reporter earns more.
first_30_days: Sign 3-5 remote-capable freelance or semi-retired reporters. Pick one county whose family departments run on Zoom and cover it manually with a shared spreadsheet and a text pager. Offer 10 solo family law attorneys and two DV appellate nonprofits (start with the Family Violence Appellate Project) at-cost coverage of their next 5 hearings. Track wait time per hearing so the prediction model has real data.

title: Verified Colony-Strength Ledger for Commercial Beekeepers
one_liner: Third-party hive-strength verification and escrowed pollination contracts, turning bees into a gradeable, financeable commodity after record die-offs.
customer: Migratory commercial beekeepers running 1,000+ hives who truck colonies to California almonds and other crops. Almond and fruit growers are the counterparties.
problem: Surveys found commercial operations lost an average of about 62% of colonies between June 2024 and February 2025, and estimated the lost almond pollination income at more than $400M. Pollination is sold by phone brokers on 'frames of bees' standards that are verified by spot manual inspection, so disputes and 'strength laundering' are common. Growers can't be sure what they get, beekeepers can't prove what they have, and lenders and insurers can't underwrite either.
solution: An inspector network using thermal imaging and frame-count sampling to grade colony strength before loading, with results stored in a tamper-evident ledger tied to each yard and hive. Strength-tiered pollination contracts with escrowed payments released on verified counts. Later, hive collateral reports for ag lenders, and parametric or indemnity cover for winter losses.
why_now: The 2024-25 losses were the worst on record, and 2025-26 survey and industry reports show continuing stress. Almond growers are paying about $181 per colony (2023 figure) for strong hives and demand certainty. Thermal and camera-based frame counting is now cheap. Almond bloom in February 2027 is about five months away, so a working pilot can earn first revenue this winter.
revenue_model: $4-8 per hive inspected, paid by the beekeeper and often co-paid by growers. A 2-3% fee on escrowed contract value. Later: data fees from ag lenders and insurance commissions.
non_obvious_insight: A beekeeper's scarcest asset is now the healthy colony, and the trade runs on trust and handshake grading. A neutral, standardized 'strength certificate' does three things at once: it lets strong operators charge more, it lets growers verify what they bought, and it creates the collateral data that lets banks lend against bees. The verifier becomes the exchange.
first_30_days: Contact 5-10 mid-size migratory beekeepers and 2-3 pollination brokers now (before winter loading). Hire or contract 2-3 experienced bee inspectors, and pilot thermal frame counting on 2,000 hives. Offer growers a paid 'verified load' program for the January-February 2027 loading window. Publish a strength-grade standard and get 2 growers to commit to tiered pricing.

title: Deepfake Shields for Mayors, Sold Through Risk Pools
angle: Pairing 2: Creator economy & media provenance x Government/public sector/defense/municipal services (long-tail likeness protection x municipal risk channel)
one_liner: Long-tail likeness and voice protection for roughly 500,000 local elected officials, clerks and first responders who have no agency to police impersonation, sold as a loss-control service through municipal insurance risk pools and county election offices.
customer: State and regional municipal risk pools and cyber pools ($300-1,500 per member per year), county election offices ($500-2,000 each), and sheriffs' and police chiefs' associations.
problem: YouTube's likeness detection reached celebrities through CAA, UTA and WME in April 2026 with no path for anyone else, and voice clones need only seconds of audio (prior knowledge). Local officials are high-impact targets: a cloned 'mayor' telling finance staff to wire funds, fake curfew or polling-place notices, fake council videos. Local IT is thin (Dallas County is cutting 31 IT staff), federal election-security help to localities was scaled back in 2025 (prior knowledge), and the midterms are Nov 3, 2026.
solution: Enroll officials with consented voice and face references and monitor major platforms using existing detection APIs. Run a human takedown desk using platform impersonation policies and state deepfake statutes. Give finance staff call-back code-word protocols and quarterly voice-clone drills, and deliver evidence packs for insurers and police.
why_now: Midterm urgency, celebrity-only platform tools, and cheap high-quality voice cloning all arrive together. Pools face rising social-engineering claims (inference), and EU Article 50 plus platform enforcement raise expectations that impersonations get pulled quickly.
revenue_model: A per-member fee paid by the pool, per-incident takedown fees, drill fees, and premium credits negotiated with the pool.
non_obvious_insight: The 'agency' that long-tail people lack is the insurance pool. It already pays social-engineering claims, has member-services budgets, and can buy for a thousand towns in one sale. Framing the product as claims reduction rather than reputation management is what unlocks the budget.
first_30_days: Interview 5 pool loss-control managers and sell a $499 election-season kit to 20 county clerks. Run a free voice-clone drill for one pool's treasurers association to produce a claim-reduction case study.

title: Agent-Populated Simulated First Job for Juniors
one_liner: A 12-week simulated first job where new grads work inside a persistent fake company staffed by AI coworkers, clients and managers, producing an auditable work record employers trust.
customer: Employers pay $4-8k per hire or subscribe to pre-screened cohorts. Universities and bootcamps pay per-seat licences ($500-1,500), and state workforce boards fund seats. Start with RevOps, FP&A or customer-success analyst roles.
problem: The bottom rung is gone. Employers don't hire juniors because AI absorbs the tasks they learned on, and internships or apprenticeships need employer bandwidth, the very thing missing. Grads can't get the experience employers demand (Stanford: 19% gap, 42% underemployment).
solution: A persistent multi-agent world with a messy CRM or ledger, a ticket queue, stakeholder agents with hidden goals who change requirements, an AI manager giving 1:1s and an on-call incident. The junior works with their own AI tools and everything is logged. Senior humans grade a few deliverables weekly. The output is a portable 'experience ledger' (hours, artifacts, review outcomes, error-detection rates) employers can inspect.
why_now: Long-horizon agent capability and multi-agent simulation now make believable coworkers affordable (Project Vend-style and TheAgentCompany-style experiments), employers say they can't evaluate candidates in AI-permitted interviews, and the freeze is widening.
revenue_model: Employer per-hire success fees and pre-screen subscriptions, university licences and modest learner fees.
non_obvious_insight: The cold start of apprenticeship marketplaces is employer supply. A simulation removes it: the employer is fake but the evaluation is real. Employers hire on traces of judgment rather than resumes, and the moat is a scenario library built from anonymised real incidents.
first_30_days: Build one role sim (RevOps analyst) with 4 agent personas. Run it with 20 recent grads via a college career centre. Get 5 mid-size SaaS employers to review the graduates' traces and commit to interviews.

title: Second Reader for Consumer Scan Anxiety
angle: Pairing 1: Healthcare delivery/GLP-1/longevity/consumer health x Mental health/loneliness/community/meaning
one_liner: An independent internist plus CBT-for-health-anxiety clinician who reads your Function, Superpower or full-body-scan results and tells you what not to chase.
customer: Members of consumer preventive-health services (blood-panel subscriptions and full-body scans), paying $99-199 per second read. Employers and the testing companies themselves come later, as white-label buyers, and only under a no-follow-up-revenue rule.
problem: Consumer preventive health is now mass market: Function has 1M+ members, Neko raised $700M for a NYC launch and Superpower just raised its price. Every result set produces borderline flags and incidental findings, which start cascades of retests and anxiety. The testing firms are diagnostic-only and paid on repeat testing, and their in-house clinicians are throughput-limited. Nobody is paid to say 'ignore this' or to treat the health anxiety the testing creates.
solution: A 45-minute second read by an internist, informed by radiology decision rules, ranks each finding as act, watch or ignore. A CBT-trained clinician adds a short protocol for uncertainty tolerance and reassurance-seeking. The member gets a one-page 'what not to chase' plan and a 30-day check-in, with optional monthly groups for chronic worriers. Simple decision trees for the top 30 flag types keep unit cost low.
why_now: Neko's US launch (July 2026), Function's $298M raise and acquisition of Ezra, and Superpower's Sep 2026 price increase are putting millions of first-time results in front of consumers at once. Mental health has been the top digital-health funding category for 7 years, so CBT clinicians are abundant and cheap to contract. LLM summaries make cheap first-pass triage possible, but they are not trusted with liability.
revenue_model: $99-199 per DTC second read, $19/month optional follow-up membership, and later a B2B2C white-label at about $6-12 per member per year to testing companies that want fewer refunds and complaints. Employers buy a capped-visit benefit.
non_obvious_insight: More testing creates a new patient, the worried well with abnormal-ish numbers, and testing companies are paid on the retest loop. An independent party paid by the patient has a credibility the vendor cannot fake. Health-anxiety CBT works, but anxious people seek doctors for reassurance, not therapists. Delivering it as a 'second opinion on your results' is the door they will walk through.
first_30_days: Contract two internists and one CBT-HA clinician part-time. Offer $99 founder-price second reads in Function and Superpower subreddits and longevity Discords. Run about 40 sessions and record pre/post anxiety scores (GAD-7 or Whiteley-7) and follow-up tests avoided. Take the outcome data to one scan center or one employer benefits broker.

title: Boundary Truth: Ledger of Special-District Lines
one_liner: Turn recorded annexation, inclusion and exclusion instruments into a single authoritative boundary ledger that catches wrong tax bills, wrong ballots and wrong 911 routing.
customer: County assessors and treasurers, election offices, state 911 boards and NG911 GIS coordinators, plus special-district management firms and metro-district law firms. Paid through the recorder's technology or preservation fund (spendable at the recorder's discretion in many states), election grant money or 911 fee funds.
problem: There are about 39,000 special districts (fire, water, library, mosquito, metro) and their boundary changes are recorded with the county clerk as ministerial filings with no downstream notification. Nobody reliably updates the assessor's tax-area codes, the election office's address-to-district crosswalk or the 911 emergency-service boundary layer. Result: parcels billed by the wrong district or by none (lost revenue, later refunds), voters handed the wrong ballot style, and dispatch mismatches. State attorneys general have issued opinions on tax levies made after officials weren't notified of boundary changes. We discover the errors in the last two weeks before an election or when a taxpayer complains.
solution: An AI pipeline reads the recorded instruments (metes-and-bounds text, plats, ordinances), draws polygons with closure and area sanity checks, and routes low-confidence ones to a human reviewer. It keeps a versioned, effective-dated ledger of each district's legal boundary. It then diffs the ledger against the assessor's tax-area file, the voter address crosswalk and the 911 boundary layer, and returns a plain exception list such as '312 parcels inside Fire District 4 per the 2022 recorded inclusion but billed to no district.' Sell a fixed-price audit first, then an annual subscription.
why_now: Mid-decade redistricting fights and the 2026 midterms have made ballot-style accuracy politically radioactive. NG911 requires clean authoritative boundary GIS data. Property tax scrutiny makes every misbilled dollar a headline. LLMs can now parse legal descriptions well enough to draft polygons that a human reviews rather than draws.
revenue_model: $15k-$40k one-time boundary drift audit per county, then $10k-$30k/year per county for continuous monitoring, sized to fit inside a recorder's technology fund or a 911 board budget. Data-quality add-ons for district management firms and bond counsel.
non_obvious_insight: The legal boundary is the recorded instrument, not the GIS layer; the layer is just someone's drawing of a PDF. Because the clerk often sits at the junction of records, elections and sometimes tax, we see the stale cascade that assessors, election staff and 911 GIS analysts each see only a slice of. Also, the clerk's tech fund often sits outside the commissioners' budget fight, so a $25k audit can be approved in weeks, not the 18 months that scares govtech investors.
first_30_days: Pick one state heavy on special districts (Colorado metro districts, Texas MUDs and ESDs, Illinois, Washington, Florida CDDs). Offer a free boundary drift audit to a single county's assessor and clerk using five years of recorded inclusions and annexations. Turn the mismatch list into a paid pilot funded from the recorder's fund, then take the proof to the state 911 board.

title: Won-Bid Price Benchmark Co-op for Cleaners
one_liner: An anonymous give-to-get database of what jobs actually sold for, so specialty cleaners and similar trades can price with market data instead of cost-plus calculators.
customer: Owner-operators of bid-priced service trades. Start with post-construction, commercial and janitorial cleaning, then pressure washing, window cleaning and junk removal. They pay $19-29/mo. Later buyers are the suppliers and insurers who want price indexes.
problem: Every month r/sweatystartup fills with the same question: "What's the going rate for commercial cleaning?", "How to price a large post-construction cleaning job (30k sqft+)", "Pricing on 55,000 sq foot machine shop cleaning", "I need help with quote calculator!", "How do you price your cleaning jobs? Looking to update my rates". The cluster scores 85/100 in an August 2026 snapshot. Calculators only give a cost-plus floor.
solution: A contribution flow accepts anonymized won and lost bids (scope, sqft, frequency, ZIP-3, price, outcome). Owners can also upload old proposal PDFs or emails, and an LLM extracts the structured fields so contributing is one step. In return they see the p25/p50/p75 price band and a win-rate curve for their scope and region. Later it adds a bid sanity check that reads quotes exported from Jobber or Housecall Pro, and a published quarterly price index.
why_now: LLM extraction from messy PDF quotes, emails and photos removes the data-entry burden that killed earlier crowd-pricing efforts. Owners now ask peers on Reddit and also ask ChatGPT, which only gives generic ranges. Rising labor and insurance costs make owners want to reprice, and they need market data to do it safely.
revenue_model: Free to contribute and see coarse bands. $19-29/mo for full bands, win curves and quote checks. Enterprise data licensing, such as a price index for distributors, insurers and franchisors, from $500/mo once there are at least 1,000 bids.
non_obvious_insight: Cost-plus tells you the price floor, not what the market paid, and that is the number people are asking about. The demand for pricing tools is huge but formula-only: the Method Clean Biz janitorial bid calculator says it has been "used by over 170,000 cleaning professionals over the past 10 years" and uses a cost-plus formula with no market data (https://methodcleanbiz.com/janitorial-bid-calculator/). Yet owners still ask peers about going rates. r/sweatystartup has six pricing threads in one snapshot (https://www.ideafast.pro/pains/sweatystartup). Nobody publishes won-bid prices, so the only way to get them is a co-op where contributors trade their own data. The business is the dataset, and the first 200 contributed bids are a moat.
first_30_days: Week 1: set up a Typeform and a Google Sheet. Answer pricing threads in r/sweatystartup and cleaning forums with "send me your last few bids anonymized and I'll send back the market band". Weeks 2-3: collect 100+ bids by doing the analysis by hand and publish a free weekly "price index" post. Week 4: ask the first 30 contributors to pay $19/mo for continued access, and start building the PDF proposal extractor.

title: Backflow Testers Roll-Up With Portal-Filing Agents
one_liner: Consolidate small backflow-test shops, then use agents to parse city notices, schedule tests and file results in each water utility's portal, turning mandated annual tests into a low-churn route business.
customer: Property managers, restaurants, car washes, medical buildings, HOAs and multifamily owners who must test backflow assemblies annually, and water utilities who benefit from compliance. Retiring tester shops are the sellers.
problem: Most jurisdictions require annual (sometimes more frequent) tests by a certified tester who submits results to the local water purveyor, and portals and forms vary by utility. Owners miss deadlines and get shutoff threats. Testers are solo or small shops using paper. A failed test triggers repairs worth several times the test fee.
solution: Buy small tester shops to build route density. AI ops: an intake agent parses utility letters and portal notices across a manager's whole portfolio, schedules the nearest tester, files results with browser-automation agents, tracks failures and sends repair quotes. Expand into other mandate-locked recurring routes such as fire extinguisher and sprinkler inspection, kitchen hood, cross-connection surveys and enhanced septic O&M.
why_now: Browser and computer-use agents can now reliably operate idiosyncratic municipal portals. Utilities are moving to online-only submission of test results, and owner-testers are aging out.
revenue_model: $75 to $150 per test, $300 to $1,500 per repair or rebuild, plus annual portfolio management fees for property managers.
non_obvious_insight: A regulator creates the demand and portal friction is the moat. Tests are the loss-leader; repairs, replacements and installs after failed tests carry the margin. Any 'city letter, must act' recurring compliance category is underserved by software, because each authority's process is different.
first_30_days: Start as a compliance concierge for 10 property managers at $15 to $25 per device per year, subcontracting the tests to local certified testers. Build the notice parser and one or two portal integrations. After the flow works, buy one tester shop (about $100k to $250k of owner earnings) on seller financing.

title: Moonlighting and IP Clearance for AI Experts
one_liner: A concierge that checks and files the employer-disclosure, IP-assignment and confidentiality paperwork professionals need before moonlighting as AI-training experts, and issues clean-provenance certificates that labs and vendors can rely on.
customer: Employed lawyers, bankers, doctors, consultants and engineers doing expert-data gigs pay $79-149 per clearance. Data vendors and lab legal or procurement teams pay for an annual B2B license.
problem: Millions of experts have signed up, many still employed at banks, law firms and hospitals with outside-activity approval rules (e.g. FINRA-registered staff), IP assignment and confidentiality duties. Some platforms even solicit prior work that former employers may own (HN Apr 2026). One trade-secret suit could freeze a vendor's programs, and workers risk termination or licence discipline.
solution: (1) A contract reader flags moonlighting, IP and confidentiality risk in the worker's agreement and handbook. (2) Templates for the employer disclosure or approval request. (3) A scanner for confidential markers in submitted work. (4) A 'clean-room certificate' per contributor. (5) An onboarding API vendors can require. A partner attorney covers the advice.
why_now: The Mercor breach and class actions have made vendor risk teams and lab counsel nervous. Reports of labs asking contractors for real past work samples raise provenance stakes. The scale of professionals moonlighting for AI companies is unprecedented.
revenue_model: Per-clearance fee for workers plus $50-250k annual vendor licences and per-contributor API fees.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer with money is the vendor's general counsel, not the worker, but the worker channel gives distribution and data. A database of moonlighting and IP policies for the top few thousand employers, built from worker submissions, becomes the moat.
first_30_days: Interview 20 moonlighting experts. Hand-build 50 employer-policy profiles (big banks, Big 4, large law firms, health systems). Run a manual $99 concierge clearance service. Pitch two mid-tier data vendors' compliance leads a paid pilot.

title: Street-Level Gas Pipe Retirement Optimizer
one_liner: Software plus a turnkey block-by-block electrification crew that tells gas utilities which streets to retire instead of replace.
customer: Regulated gas distribution utilities in MA, NY, CO, MN, WA, CA and IL, and their regulators. Funding comes from pipe-replacement capex budgets.
problem: Electrification shrinks gas throughput, so fixed pipe costs land on fewer customers. Utilities still replace leak-prone mains at millions of dollars per mile. Regulators (for example Massachusetts DPU 20-80-B) demand non-pipeline alternatives, but nobody optimizes at street-segment level. Heat pump quotes run ~$9,000 and labor is scarce.
solution: GIS, billing and housing-stock analytics that score each pipe segment for retire-versus-replace, and find streets where electrifying 30-80 homes costs less than replacing the main. Then deliver the electrification block by block: group purchase, one crew per street per week, optionally networked geothermal. It is filed as a utility non-pipeline alternative.
why_now: State non-pipeline-alternative orders and thermal-energy-network laws are in force. With federal credits dead, utility-funded programs are the only scaled electrification channel. Ratepayer affordability pressure makes stranded pipe a live issue.
revenue_model: $250-500k a year SaaS per utility plus a per-home program fee ($5-12k) paid from avoided pipe capex.
non_obvious_insight: Gas utilities' problem is no longer selling heat pumps. It is stranded pipe. Their pipe replacement capex is the electrification budget hiding in plain sight.
first_30_days: Model one Massachusetts or New York utility territory from public leak-prone-pipe, assessor and census data. Publish a 'retire-first streets' list for one city. Pitch a city sustainability office, a regulator and two utility strategy VPs. Sell a $60-100k pilot analysis.

title: Consolidation Shock Radar for Independent Clinics
one_liner: Every roll-up creates a wave of unhappy clients and departing staff near the acquired clinic; sell independents, would-be founders and lenders a radar that finds those neighborhoods first.
customer: Independent and affordable-care clinics (client win-back and recruiting), DVMs leaving corporate to open practices, and practice lenders or equipment lessors.
problem: GoodVets is buying WellHaven (75 to 116 locations, announced 2026-09-24), and Mars runs about 2,100 clinics. After a deal, prices, hours and staffing change, but nearby independents have no signal about where clients and staff are becoming loose. De novo founders pick sites by gut feel and lenders lack local competitive data.
solution: Track acquisitions using state facility records, Google Business Profile and website changes ('now part of...'), price-list scrapes, review-sentiment shifts and job-posting churn. Deliver (a) an alert plus a ready-to-send 'neighbor clinic' welcome campaign and records-transfer kit for independents within 5 miles, (b) recruiting lists of departing DVMs and techs, and (c) site-scoring reports for lenders and de novo founders.
why_now: Continuous roll-ups (GoodVets/WellHaven this week), visits reportedly falling three years running, and corporate chains structurally unable to cut price. Open web data plus LLM extraction makes the tracking cheap for a two-person team.
revenue_model: $199-499 per month per clinic by radius, $2-5K per de novo site report, and a lender API subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Consolidation is discussed as a scale story. The neglected consequence is local displacement: the buyer's own integration changes service and pricing at a known date, which opens a recurring window for competitors. That window is a sellable time-series signal nobody packages.
first_30_days: Build scrapers for 3 states. Identify 30 clinics acquired in the last 12 months. Cold-email 100 independents within 5 miles with a 'your neighborhood's acquired clinics' one-pager. Aim to sell 5 subscriptions at $299 per month.

title: PTO Bureau: Cash Advances Priced on Utility Delay
one_liner: A data co-op plus bridge lender that advances the 10-20% held back until utility Permission-to-Operate, and prices each advance from real per-utility delay history.
customer: Small and mid-size residential installers doing about 50-500 systems a year ($2-15M revenue). Their cash is squeezed post-25D. Secondary buyers are TPO sponsors and developers who need systems energized before the Dec 31, 2027 placed-in-service cliff.
problem: Lenders and TPO sponsors release most of the money at install but hold back the final 10-20% until PTO. Installer-reported PTO waits run 4-12 weeks, and about 8-12 weeks for battery systems in SCE territory. That holdback is often the entire gross margin, so an installer with 60-100 unenergized systems is one supplier-credit squeeze from insolvency. For TPO systems that did not begin construction by July 4, 2026, the 30% 48E credit requires placed-in-service by Dec 31, 2027, and tax-equity investors generally treat PTO as that trigger. Every idle week is now worth real money to sponsors.
solution: Three pieces. (1) A PTO clock: a member-contributed dataset of submit-to-PTO days by utility, AHJ, system size, and whether it includes storage, plus the recurring deficiency-notice reasons. (2) Bridge advances: buy or advance against the PTO holdback within 48 hours of a passed final inspection, priced from the clock, for example 3-6% for a system expected under 60 days. (3) PTO SWAT: a human team with utility-portal expertise that fixes and re-submits deficient interconnection packages, sold per system, and sold to sponsors as a deadline bounty for clearing backlog before the 2027 cutoff.
why_now: 25D expired Dec 31, 2025 and TPO is now the main route to a federal credit. The 48E begin-construction window closed July 4, 2026, so the 12/31/2027 placed-in-service deadline is now the binding constraint. Storm and battery-heavy interconnection queues are growing, and NEC 2026 adoption is adding deficiency notices. Traditional lenders are pulling back from small installers after the 2025-26 failures.
revenue_model: Discount fee on advances, roughly 25-40% annualized. A $150-300 per-system SWAT fee. Sponsor-paid bounties for pre-deadline energization. A later license of the PTO clock dataset to lenders, tax-equity investors and utilities.
non_obvious_insight: PTO delay looks random to outsiders but is predictable, because it comes from a few utility reviewer queues and about ten repeat deficiency reasons: single-line diagram mismatches, label errors, battery configuration and inverter list issues. Installers know their own utility's clock, but nobody has pooled it. A tiny lender that underwrites on predicted PTO days can beat big finance companies. The collateral is also better than it looks, because the system is already built and has passed the local inspection.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 installers in a single utility territory. Trade a free benchmark report for their last 12 months of PTO timestamps. Publish the resulting utility PTO clock as a lead magnet. Line up a $250-500k line from a community lender or family office. Fund the first 20 advances at installers that sell directly to a sponsor, where assignment consent is easiest. Run the SWAT service as a manual concierge for $200 per system to learn the deficiency patterns.
